seo_title: Cost of Living in Kuala Lumpur 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Kuala Lumpur per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A tropical metropolis with the MM2H programme — a long-term visa for remote workers. English is everywhere, ultra-modern towers stand next to Asian markets, and the region's best private schools and healthcare are here.
pros: The MM2H programme — a long-term visa for remote workers and investors
English everywhere — a low language barrier
The developed infrastructure of an Asian capital: metro, malls, healthcare
Direct flights to Russia and access to all of Asia
cons: A tropical climate with high humidity year-round
Hard to manage without a car or Grab — distances are large
A traditional local society (a Muslim country)
MM2H was tightened in 2024 — the deposit rose to 1 mln ringgit

visa_steps.title: Tourist entry
visa_steps.description: Up to 30 days visa-free on a passport. Extendable at immigration for 30 days.

visa_steps.title: DE Rantau (Digital Nomad)
visa_steps.description: A visa for remote workers earning from 24,000 dollars a year. A 1-year residence permit, renewable.

visa_steps.title: MM2H Visa
visa_steps.description: A long-term visa for the financially independent: a deposit from 1 mln ringgit and active income from 40,000 ringgit a month.

visa_steps.title: Tax ID (Income Tax File)
visa_steps.description: Set up at LHDN after getting the visa. Needed for a bank account and official work.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Maybank, CIMB and RHB open accounts with a visa and a lease. Cards work across Southeast Asia.

faq.question: Why bother with MM2H if there's DE Rantau in Kuala Lumpur?
faq.answer: MM2H runs 5–10 years with the right to buy property. DE Rantau is simpler and faster, but only for 1 year.

faq.question: What about children in Kuala Lumpur?
faq.answer: Top international schools: Mont Kiara International, Garden, Alice Smith. From 13,000 dollars a year.

faq.question: Is the climate hard to handle in Kuala Lumpur?
faq.answer: Hot (+27–32°C) and humid year-round, with frequent downpours. Air conditioning is a must.

faq.question: Where should I live in Kuala Lumpur?
faq.answer: Bangsar — expats and hipsters. Mont Kiara — families. KLCC — the very centre and work. Sri Hartamas — quiet.

faq.question: What about alcohol and food in Kuala Lumpur?
faq.answer: Malaysia is a Muslim country, but alcohol is sold in most districts. Pork is only in Chinese and Western restaurants.

faq.question: Can I work for Western companies in Kuala Lumpur?
faq.answer: Yes, on DE Rantau or MM2H. Tax for non-residents is 30%, for residents up to 24% progressively.

reviews.text: We got DE Rantau as a family and moved from Bangkok. School in Mont Kiara, Gleneagles for healthcare, a house in Bangsar. KL is easier than Bangkok and the infrastructure is cleaner.
I work for a Singapore startup. I rent a studio in KLCC with a view of the towers for 800 dollars. People speak English everywhere, the visa is simple, and the climate is bearable.
